slides.title: Requirement-Driven Design of Whole-Body Social Tactile Sensing via Virtual Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework to derive tactile sensing requirements from interaction data, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: A requirement-driven framework using VR to determine optimal tactile sensor placement and resolution for social robots.
card.key_idea: VR-based interaction data is collected and offline-reconstructed to simulate various tactile sensor configurations, decoupling sensing requirements from hardware constraints before physical fabrication.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via two user studies (12 and 18 participants) and a 5,520-trial dataset using Random Forest and CNN-GRU classifiers with leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
card.limitation: Simulation uses only binary contact signals (no force/pressure) and resolution analysis was limited to the robot's arm.

slides.title: Representation-Aligned Tactile Grounding for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
slides.highlight: This research introduces a Latent Tactile Predictor (LTP) that aligns intermediate action representations with future contact consequences to improve contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: Improves contact-rich robotic manipulation by aligning future tactile prediction with intermediate action-expert representations.
card.key_idea: Uses linear probes to identify an intermediate representation for a Latent Tactile Predictor (LTP), which supervises action-conditioned contact dynamics using compact tactile latents.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real-world tasks using SmolVLA and π0 backbones; achieved 74% and 73% average success, outperforming VLM-side and final-state grounding.

slides.title: Never Too Late for Force: Accelerating VLA Post-Training with Reactive Force Injection
slides.highlight: This work introduces LIFT, a framework that adds contact reactivity to pretrained VLA policies via force injection and online corrective data, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: LIFT adds reactive force feedback to pretrained VLAs to improve contact-rich manipulation without losing general knowledge.
card.key_idea: Grafts a reactive action expert with causal force memory and zero-initialized cross-attention, trained via online DAgger on mixed offline visual and online force-enabled data.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement; LIFT achieved higher peak performance and faster learning than vision-only baselines.
card.limitation: Depends on human corrections during online DAgger, limiting data throughput; evaluated only on single-arm manipulation.

slides.title: Catch, Throw, Repeat: Planning for Human-Robot Partner Juggling
slides.highlight: This work presents a planning and control architecture for synchronized multi-ball juggling, advancing physical human-robot interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: A real-time planning architecture enabling a robot to reliably partner-juggle multi-ball patterns with humans.
card.key_idea: Combines predictive Kalman-filter ball tracking, adaptive online trajectory optimization via multiple-shooting, and a state-machine coordination logic to manage catch-and-throw decisions.
card.evaluation: User study with 8 participants (novice to expert); achieved 3-ball cascades, with one participant reaching 20 consecutive catches. Results are supported by MuJoCo simulations.
card.limitation: Performance is constrained by timing pressure at high ball counts and lack of explicit spatial coordination to avoid inter-ball collisions.

slides.title: MIDAS Hand: Modular low-Impedance Direct-drive Anthropomorphic Sensing Hand
slides.highlight: The MIDAS Hand provides a human-scale platform with integrated tactile sensing and low backdrive torque, supporting the human-to-robot data collection and physics-based sensing needs of MOSAIC.

card.one_liner: A low-cost, open-source, human-scale dexterous hand featuring direct-drive actuation and integrated multi-axis tactile sensing.
card.key_idea: Combines 13 active DoFs, 3D-printed modular construction, and 283 three-axis tactile taxels with low-friction rigid linkages for high backdrivability and ease of maintenance.
card.evaluation: Validated via GRASP taxonomy (32/33 types), backdrive torque tests, 5,000+ cycle reliability tests, and teleoperation demos. Results show high repeatability (0.016mm std dev).
card.limitation: Lacks a little finger, limiting specific ulnar-side grasps; tactile sensing is currently demonstrated as a modality, not yet in closed-loop control.

slides.title: Robust In-Hand Manipulation via Priors in Reinforcement Learning and Mechanical Design
slides.highlight: This work introduces global grasp-quality and local contact-geometry priors to enhance rotation efficiency and stability in multifingered robotic manipulation.

card.one_liner: Improves robust in-hand rotation by combining grasp-quality RL rewards with anisotropic fingertip mechanical design.
card.key_idea: Integrates a global grasp-quality prior as a dense RL reward and a local contact-geometry prior via cylindrical fingertip morphology to stabilize rolling and reduce off-axis drift.
card.evaluation: Tested on cylinders, cuboids, and balls across four palm orientations using proprioception. Metrics included rotation speed, episode duration, and success rate in simulation and real-world.
card.limitation: Not evaluated on translation or tool-use; robustness only tested via gravity changes rather than direct external perturbations; sim-to-real transfer not quantified.

slides.title: Towards Human-like Physical Intelligence: Lifelong Vision-Language-Action Learning for Robotic Manipulation
slides.tldr: LIFELONG VLA LEARNING FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: The LifelongVLA framework addresses the plasticity-stability trade-off in robotic manipulation using a dual-timescale adaptation mechanism and a cache-efficient replay strategy.

card.one_liner: LifelongVLA enables robots to sequentially learn new manipulation skills while minimizing catastrophic forgetting of previous tasks.
card.key_idea: Uses a dual-timescale LoRA gating module to balance plasticity and stability, combined with a cache-efficient stochastic replay strategy using compact latent prefix tokens.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 10 LIBERO benchmark tasks and real-world xArm robot; outperformed baselines with 83.2% average success rate and 11.4% forgetting rate.
card.limitation: Evaluation is limited in task scale and diversity; may struggle with very long task streams or ambiguous, conversational user instructions.

slides.title: DiMaS: Distribution Matching for Steering Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.tldr: DISTRIBUTION-MATCHING FOR FINE-GRAINED VLA BEHAVIORAL CONTROL
slides.highlight: DiMaS introduces a distribution-matching steering strategy for flow-matching VLAs, enabling more effective behavioral control than traditional linear steering methods.

card.one_liner: DiMaS enables fine-grained behavioral control in flow-matching VLAs via distribution-matching representation steering.
card.key_idea: Unlike linear steering, DiMaS transports between representation distributions to control behavior, addressing the fact that visuomotor features are linearly decodable but not linearly steerable.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on two state-of-the-art VLAs, testing behavioral control and generalizability across increasingly dissimilar tasks.
card.limitation: Behavioral control weakens as the tasks used for learning and evaluation become more dissimilar.
